content.title: Symbolic Layout, Single Move | Embodied System Consequence
content.summary: Travel inside an original symbolic layout at marker height before revealing a much larger entity or machine bound to it. Introduce one external manipulator while the comparison layout stays fixed, move exactly one identifiable marker with visible contact and end on one restrained state change in the bound full-scale system.

quick_start.input_format: object-height travel through an original symbolic layout + reveal a larger entity or system causally bound to the layout + one external hand or manipulator enters while comparison markers stay fixed + move exactly one identifiable marker with visible contact + one restrained state change proves the larger consequence
quick_start.recommended_input: Track between frosted-glass lens markers toward a dormant full-scale lighthouse engine, reveal their copper wiring, then let an adult technician move one obsidian lens disk into an empty ring. One pulse reaches the engine, which opens a single iris and holds one white beam across the same chamber.
required_anchors: Travel through an original symbolic layout at marker height before revealing its larger system.
Bind the layout to one much larger entity, machine or environment in a single wide reveal.
Change exactly one clearly identifiable marker and show contact.
End on one restrained state change in the bound system.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Travel inside an original symbolic layout at marker height before revealing a much larger entity or machine bound to it. Introduce one external manipulator while the comparison layout stays fixed, move exactly one identifiable marker with visible contact and end on one restrained state change in the bound full-scale system.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Begin inside an original symbolic layout at object height so its markers read as spatial architecture before revealing a much larger entity or machine causally bound to that layout. Introduce one external hand or manipulator, keep the surrounding configuration stable, and change exactly one clearly identifiable marker. Do not add a second move. End with one restrained, observable state change in the bound full-scale entity or environment that proves the small intervention altered a larger system. The reusable mechanism is layout-as-world, scale reveal, single deliberate intervention and embodied consequence—not the source chess pieces, king, board, armored hand, crown, palace, fantasy design, exact move, camera route, color treatment, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Travel through an original symbolic layout at marker height before revealing its larger system.
invariants.purpose: Lets the audience experience the abstract arrangement as a physical world.
invariants.ablation_failure: A top-down diagram alone cannot establish the later scale reversal.

invariants.rule: Bind the layout to one much larger entity, machine or environment in a single wide reveal.
invariants.purpose: Makes later symbolic intervention consequential beyond the tabletop.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a bound system, moving a marker remains decorative.

invariants.rule: Introduce one external hand or manipulator while surrounding markers remain stable.
invariants.purpose: Identifies a deliberate decision-maker and preserves comparison context.
invariants.ablation_failure: Many simultaneous changes obscure agency and causality.

invariants.rule: Change exactly one clearly identifiable marker and show contact.
invariants.purpose: Creates one readable strategic cause instead of a montage of operations.
invariants.ablation_failure: A hidden or multiple move cannot be mapped to the final result.

invariants.rule: End on one restrained state change in the bound system.
invariants.purpose: Confirms the larger consequence without replacing the idea with spectacle.
invariants.ablation_failure: No response leaves the symbolic action unresolved; excessive action hides the causal link.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source black and white chess pieces, board squares, exact arrangement, move and checkmate implication
the source seated king-like ruler, face, crown, armor, cloak, throne, hand and glowing-eye treatment
the source palace-scale chess world, armies, architecture, snow or particles and fantasy iconography
the source low chess traversal, central reveal, macro hand move, facial close-up, timing and cinematic rendering
the source creator identity, LouieVerse naming, NANOCINEMA text, watermark, prompt-sharing claim and branding
